ARC-01.evidence: Lists and filters run as relational queries on one table per DocType (frappe/model/db_query.py), not a generic store; definitions drive indexes: DocField/Custom Field search_index -> ADD INDEX (frappe/database/schema.py:105, frappe/database/mariadb/schema.py:87-96), unique indexes likewise; caching in Redis and client_cache (frappe/tests/test_caching.py, test_client_cache.py). Tested: frappe/tests/test_db_update.py and test_db.py exercise search_index. No query cost limits (level 4).

ARC-02.evidence: Declarative schema sync from DocType definitions plus forward-only patches (frappe/patches.txt, frappe/migrate.py:140 run_schema_updates); runtime DocType edits use the same DbTable.sync (frappe/database/schema.py:44). No down steps; ALTER TABLE runs directly (frappe/database/mariadb/schema.py:166-180) with only lowered lock timeouts (frappe/migrate.py:233-240); removed fields keep their columns (expand-only by default). No expand-and-contract tooling or rollback path.
ARC-02.alt_note: Non-destructive declarative sync (dropped fields keep columns, maintenance mode, lock-timeout guard) and upgrade tests (frappe/tests/test_v16_upgrade.py) behave much like a managed framework even without down steps

ARC-03.evidence: Multiple gunicorn workers and hosts supported; sessions and caches in Redis (frappe/sessions.py, frappe/cache_manager.py); but files live on local disk under sites/<site>/public|private/files, the scheduler is a single process guarded by a local FileLock (frappe/utils/scheduler.py:40-60), and client_cache is in-process with invalidation. No replica manifests or scale-out tests in repo.

ARC-04.evidence: RQ job queues with per-queue timeouts (frappe/utils/background_jobs.py:99-126), dedup by job_id (:165-188), retries on deadlock/timeout up to 5 (:337-366), failed-job registry and RQ Job/RQ Worker doctypes for visibility; automation outbox with attempts and max_attempts (frappe/automation_engine/drainer.py:126-131). Back-off is linear, idempotency is not general, and scheduler exclusivity is a host-local file lock.
ARC-04.alt_note: Automation engine outbox is durable with attempts, stale-row requeue (drainer.py:278) and effects-delivered markers (queue.py:35-47), close to idempotent and dead-lettered; tested by frappe/automation_engine/tests/test_drainer.py, test_outbox.py and frappe/tests/test_background_jobs.py

ARC-05.evidence: Site-per-database tenancy (frappe/app.py:191) gives data separation; per-site request budget via conf.rate_limit (frappe/rate_limiter.py:15-19) and concurrency limits (frappe/concurrency_limiter.py:82). Workers, Redis and scheduler are shared across sites; no noisy-neighbour detection or isolation tests found in frappe/tests.

ARC-06.evidence: frappe/tests/test_perf.py (query-count and timing assertions) and frappe/tests/microbenchmarks run in the normal suite; bundle-size workflow .github/workflows/default-js-bundle-size.yml. No documented per-surface limits.

ARC-07.evidence: Default: only /api/method/ping (frappe/__init__.py:1478). Request timing logs exist only when conf.monitor is set (frappe/monitor.py:22-24) and Sentry only with a DSN; no published objectives or alert rules in repo.

ARC-08.evidence: Webhooks have timeouts (default 5s) and scheduled retries with exhaustion (frappe/integrations/doctype/webhook/webhook.py:206-300); automation webhooks guarded with timeouts and a per-rule circuit breaker that auto-disables after consecutive failures (frappe/automation_engine/runner.py:603-620, actions/core.py:350-382, 532-541). Apps (plugins) run in-process with no isolation; Redis/DB failures take down all sites; no fault-injection tests.
